title: Regular two-cocycles of a split diagonalizable group are coboundaries
statement:
Let $R$ be any commutative ring, $M$ a finitely generated additive abelian group, and $D=D_R(M)$ [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. Write $B=R[M]$, with $\Delta(e_m)=e_m\otimes e_m$ and $\epsilon(e_m)=1$. Let $E$ be any $R$-module equipped with an $R$-linear coaction $\tau:E\to E\otimes_RB$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] satisfying $(\tau\otimes1)\tau=(1\otimes\Delta)\tau$ and $(1\otimes\epsilon)\tau=1_E$. For a commutative $R$-algebra $T$ and $h\in D(T)$, evaluating the $B$-factor in $\tau$ at $h:B\to T$ defines the action $h\mathbin{\cdot}(-)$ on $E\otimes_RT$. Put $C^n=E\otimes_R B^{\otimes n}$ for $n\geq1$. For $c\in C^n$, its evaluation $c(h_1,\ldots,h_n)$ uses the algebra maps $h_i:B\to T$ and multiplication in $T$; these evaluations define the regular cochain formulas below. Suppose $c\in C^2$ satisfies
$$h\mathbin{\cdot}c(k,l)-c(hk,l)+c(h,kl)-c(h,k)=0\quad\text{in }C^3,$$
where the expression is evaluated on the universal triple of $D$-points over $B^{\otimes3}$. Then there exists $b\in C^1$ such that
$$c(h,k)=h\mathbin{\cdot}b(k)-b(hk)+b(h)\quad\text{in }C^2,$$
with the equality evaluated on the universal pair over $B\otimes_RB$. No flatness, finite-generation or projectivity condition is imposed on $E$, and torsion in $M$ is allowed even when its order is not invertible in $R$.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes (2014), Appendix B.2, definition of the regular Hochschild cochain complex, printed pp.283-284; Lemma B.2.3 and Remark B.2.4, printed p.285, degree-two consequence of the higher-cohomology vanishing for quasi-coherent modules of diagonalizable groups. Online source read; WANTED local archive literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf.

proof.text: Define the $R$-linear map $\lambda:B\to R$ by $\lambda(\sum_m r_me_m)=r_0$, using the finitely supported basis in [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. Then $\lambda(1_B)=1_R$ and $(1_B\otimes\lambda)\Delta(f)=\lambda(f)1_B$: on $e_m$ both sides are $e_0$ if $m=0$ and zero otherwise, so the equality follows by linearity. The map on the tensor product is defined by the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Appendix B.2, regular cochain formulas on printed p.284 and diagonalizable vanishing in Remark B.2.4 on printed p.285; explicit degree-two coefficient calculation by O4.

proof.text: Put $P=1_E\otimes1_B\otimes\lambda:C^2\to C^1$ and $b=P(c)$. This is a regular cochain, defined by an $R$-linear map of the actual tensor modules. On a generator $x\otimes a\otimes f$, the four unsigned terms of the given cocycle identity are respectively $\tau(x)\otimes a\otimes f$, $x\otimes\Delta(a)\otimes f$, $x\otimes a\otimes\Delta(f)$ and $x\otimes a\otimes f\otimes1_B$. These formulas are precisely evaluation at the universal triple: multiplication of two universal points pulls a function back by $\Delta$, and omission inserts $1_B$.

source.place: Appendix B.2, regular cochain formulas on printed p.284 and diagonalizable vanishing in Remark B.2.4 on printed p.285; explicit degree-two coefficient calculation by O4.

proof.text: Apply $Q=1_E\otimes1_B\otimes1_B\otimes\lambda:C^3\to C^2$. On the four terms of step 2 its values are $\lambda(f)\tau(x)\otimes a$, $\lambda(f)x\otimes\Delta(a)$, $\lambda(f)x\otimes a\otimes1_B$ and $x\otimes a\otimes f$, respectively; the third uses step 1 and the fourth uses $\lambda(1_B)=1_R$. Since pure tensors generate and all maps are $R$-linear, their values on $c$ are therefore $h\mathbin{\cdot}b(k)$, $b(hk)$, $b(h)$ and $c(h,k)$ as elements of $C^2$. This is an equality of tensor maps, not a test only on $R$-valued points.

source.place: Appendix B.2, regular cochain formulas on printed p.284 and diagonalizable vanishing in Remark B.2.4 on printed p.285; explicit degree-two coefficient calculation by O4.

proof.text: The cocycle hypothesis and linearity of $Q$ now give $0=h\mathbin{\cdot}b(k)-b(hk)+b(h)-c(h,k)$ in $C^2$. Rearranging proves the required coboundary formula with the $b$ of step 2. All maps were constructed from finite sums, tensor bilinearity, $\tau$ and $\Delta$; the calculation uses neither division nor any exactness of tensoring, so it applies to arbitrary $E$ and to torsion in $M$ in all characteristics.

source.place: Appendix B.2, regular cochain formulas on printed p.284 and diagonalizable vanishing in Remark B.2.4 on printed p.285; explicit degree-two coefficient calculation by O4.
